prompt:
Role and task instructions:
You are a helpful, respectful and honest assistant.

User request:
[Goal] Practice playing the instrument.
[Condition] You are unable to read sheet music
[Initial plan] Choose an Instrument > Learn Basic Terminology > Start with Simple Songs > Experiment with Melodies > Stay Consistent
[Problem] You find the plan quite vague and miss necessary steps.

For a given goal, make the plan more comprehensive and concrete. For each step you plan to take, mark with '[Step xx]'.
answer:
# Practice Plan: Learning an Instrument Without Sheet Music

Sheet music is not a prerequisite — tabs, chord charts, numbered notation (jianpu), and learning by ear cover the same ground. The plan below replaces "learn terminology" and "simple songs" with concrete, testable actions.

## Phase 1 — Setup (Days 1–3)

**[Step 01] Choose exactly one instrument, using fixed criteria.** Pick an instrument that has a strong non-notation learning path, is cheap enough to buy this week, and can be practiced quietly. Recommended: ukulele (easiest first chords, cheap, tab-rich) or a 61-key keyboard (visual, Synthesia-style videos). Decide in one sitting and write the choice down — do not compare further.

**[Step 02] Buy/borrow the minimum kit.** Instrument, tuner app (e.g. any free chromatic tuner), metronome app, a stand or case, picks if guitar/ukulele, headphones if keyboard. Total budget target: under $150. No accessories beyond this list until Step 09.

**[Step 03] Lock a practice slot and a log.** Set a recurring 15-minute slot, 5 days a week, at a fixed time (e.g. 20:30). Create a one-line log: date, minutes, what you practiced, one thing that improved. Rule: a "no-zero day" is 5 minutes minimum, even if you only tune and strum once.

## Phase 2 — Terminology With a Fixed Syllabus (Days 4–10)

**[Step 04] Learn this exact 18-term list, not "basic terminology."** String, fret, nut, bridge, tuning peg, chord, root note, major vs. minor, octave, scale, key, beat, bar, tempo (BPM), downstroke/upstroke, tab line, capo, arpeggio. Use flashcards, 10 min/day for 3 days. Done when you can define 15 of 18 from memory and point to each physical part on your instrument.

**[Step 05] Learn posture and tuning as a repeatable routine.** 5 minutes: sit/stand correctly, wrist and thumb position, then tune all strings to the tuner. Also learn to check one string against another by ear. Done when tuning takes under 2 minutes unaided.

**[Step 06] Learn the notation substitute you will actually use.** For guitar/ukulele: how to read tab (lines = strings, numbers = frets, read left to right). For keyboard: jianpu (1–7 = do–ti) or falling-note videos. Spend 3 days decoding 5 short tab/notation examples before playing them. Done when you can say the note names aloud from a tab line without playing.

## Phase 3 — First Reliable Sounds (Weeks 2–3)

**[Step 07] Rhythm before notes.** With one open string or one key, play quarter notes for 60 seconds at 60 BPM, then eighth notes, then alternate. Done when you stay with the click for 2 minutes without drifting.

**[Step 08] Learn 4 chords (or a 5-note scale on keyboard).** Guitar/ukulele: e.g. C, G, Am, F (or the easiest 4 for your instrument). Keyboard: C major 5-finger position. Done when each chord rings cleanly with no muted strings, 10 times in a row.

**[Step 09] Drill chord changes against the metronome.** Switch between two chords on beat 1, then every 2 beats. Done when you can make 8 clean changes in 60 seconds at 60 BPM. Add the other chord pairs until all four connect.

## Phase 4 — Simple Songs, Chosen by Rule (Weeks 3–6)

**[Step 10] Select 3 songs by explicit criteria.** (a) one 2-chord song, (b) one 4-chord song, (c) one melody-only song you can hum. Familiar, slow, and tab/chord-chart available. Examples: "Twinkle Twinkle" (melody), "Knockin' on Heaven's Door" or "Horse With No Name" (2 chords), any 4-chord pop song you already know. Write the three titles down before practicing.

**[Step 11] Learn song (a) in 4-bar chunks.** Loop one 4-bar section at 50% tempo, 10 clean repetitions, then join sections. Done when you play the whole song start-to-finish at 70% tempo without stopping.

**[Step 12] Repeat the same chunk method for songs (b) and (c).** Two weeks each. Done when each is playable end-to-end at 80% tempo.

**[Step 13] Record yourself once a week.** 60-second phone recording, listen back against the original, and write down exactly one fix for next week (e.g. "F chord buzzes — press closer to the fret"). This is your feedback loop in place of a teacher.

## Phase 5 — Ear Skills, Your Sheet-Music Replacement (Ongoing, 5 min/session)

**[Step 14] Start interval and chord-quality training.** 5 minutes per session: hear two notes and say "same/higher/lower," then major vs. minor chord. Use a free ear-training app. Done when you identify major vs. minor correctly 8 out of 10 times.

**[Step 15] Transcribe one melody phrase by ear.** Hum a phrase, find the first note on the instrument, then the next, until the phrase matches. Start with 4 notes. Done when you can work out a full 8-note phrase unaided within 15 minutes.

## Phase 6 — Experimentation Made Concrete (Weeks 6–10)

**[Step 16] Improvise with constraints, 5 min per session.** Over a 2-chord loop, play only notes from your 5-note scale. Weekly constraints: (1) only 3 notes, (2) only long notes, (3) question-and-answer phrases (4 bars play, 4 bars rest). Done when you can improvise 2 minutes without stopping and without losing the beat.

**[Step 17] Compose and keep a "lick library."** Write one 4-bar melody per week, record it, and note its chord loop. Keep a folder of 10 ideas by Week 10. Done when you have 10 recorded snippets you could reuse.

## Phase 7 — Consistency and Review

**[Step 18] Run a fixed 20-minute session template.** 3 min tune + warm-up, 5 min chord/scale drill with metronome, 7 min current song chunks, 5 min ear training or improvisation. Use this every session so you never have to decide what to do.

**[Step 19] Do a 10-minute weekly review.** Check the log: which days were missed and why, which "done when" criteria were met, one fix carried from the recording. Adjust only one variable per week (tempo, song, or drill).

**[Step 20] Test at 30/60/90 days against measurable milestones.** Day 30: 4 clean chords + one song end-to-end. Day 60: three songs + 8-of-10 ear test. Day 90: 2 minutes of improvisation + 10 recorded ideas. If a milestone is missed, cut the tempo by 20% and repeat that phase rather than adding new material.

## Guardrails

- **Pain or buzzing:** stop the drill, check hand position (Step 05) before adding practice time.
- **Plateau lasting 2 weeks:** drop to 50% tempo and shrink the chunk to 2 bars instead of quitting the song.
- **Motivation dip:** switch to the improvisation step (Step 16) for one session — it always produces sound and keeps the streak alive.
- **Don't add a fifth chord, a new song, or new gear until the current step's "done when" is met.** Vague plans fail by adding breadth; this one advances by passing checks.
